ruleName: Repair of Damage on Putting Green
imagePrompt: A modern, semi-realistic (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised) illustration in a junior golf quiz style, showing a female golfer (Lucy) on the fringe of a green. Her ball is clearly on the fringe, just off the putting green, and she is preparing to repair a visible pitch mark located on the green, directly between her ball and the hole. The golf hole is visible, showing her intended line of play passes over the pitch mark. The setting is a well-kept golf green and surrounding fringe area. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A female golfer standing on the fringe just off the green, preparing to repair a pitch mark on the putting green between her ball and the hole.

sceneSpec.setting: Golf course putting green and fringe area
sceneSpec.players: One female golfer (Lucy), preparing to putt
sceneSpec.ballPosition: The ball lies on the fringe, just off the edge of the green
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: Lucy is about to repair a visible pitch mark on the putting green that is on her line of play towards the hole
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Show that a player may repair pitch marks on the green even if the ball is off the green
mustShow: Lucy's ball clearly lying on the fringe
A visible pitch mark on the green directly between Lucy's ball and the hole
Hole in view to establish intended line of play
Lucy preparing to repair the pitch mark

questions.title: Fixing A Pitch Mark On The Putting Green
questions.question: Lucy’s ball is just next to the green and she wants to putt. There is a small dent (pitch mark) on the grass of the green where she wants to roll her ball. Can Lucy fix the dent before she putts?

choices.text: Only if another player says it’s okay.
Only if her ball is on the green, too.

questions.explanation: Lucy can fix a pitch mark on the green, even if her ball is not on the green. Anyone can fix damage on the green if it’s in their way.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short, smooth grass around the hole where you putt.
A small dent in the green made by a ball landing on it.
The slightly longer grass just next to the green.

questions.teachingTip: Let children try fixing pitch marks with a repair tool during practice so they know how to do it gently.
likelyMisconceptions: Some may think only the person whose ball made the dent can fix it.
Some may believe you can only fix the green after you putt, not before.
Kids might think you can only fix a pitch mark if your ball is also on the green.

questions.title: Repairing Pitch Marks on the Putting Green
questions.question: Lucy's ball lies on the fringe and she intends to putt. There is a pitch mark on her line of play, and the pitch mark itself is on the putting green. May Lucy repair it?

choices.text: Only with the agreement of another player.
Only if her ball also lies on the green.

questions.explanation: Lucy is allowed to repair damage such as pitch marks on the putting green, even if her ball is not on the green. The Rules permit the repair of damage on the green that is on the line of play for any player, regardless of where their ball lies.
